items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: So as I say largely through Ken I was introduced to Carl and I ended up getting signed by Concord.

ctx.x: To an extent, although I think the more adventuresome stuff that I’ve done has not been recorded. Some of it I’m starting to. Again, to back up, it’s 1985 when I was working with Benny Goodman and almost all my work was in that swing-Dixieland kind of stuff. I financed my own first record, just saved up I think it was $5,000, and hired, got Mike Brecker and Jim McNealy and John Goldsby, Kenny Washington and did all originals in a modern context. That was my first record. And it got — I still — in some ways I…

wherever it was, whenever it was reviewed. But it led to absolutely nothing in the way of work. No jobs, no nothing. Couldn’t get into clubs, nobody was hiring me as a sideman, nothing, nothing. So I continued working, getting more and more established in this vein, and also traveling to Europe, getting more established over there everywhere as this mainstream trumpet player. Then by the early 90s — so I’m working with like the younger guys I’m working are some of the guys who are here — Ken Peplowski, Howard…

tune I think we did was that “Lullaby of Broadway.” And surprising enough he liked it, and he heard Ray Anderson and he said, “Wow, this guy’s great.” Which was really nice that I felt like he sort of trusted me and if he heard it and he heard that there was some integrity to it, that he would go along with it. So that was encouraging. Then a short year after that he died. And so now the company is kind of going through a little bit of financial insanity but supposedly everything is going to continue.
